description: A customer's excess is their share minus the average share, divided by the average share.

c.request: Total up each customer's invoice totals and work out each customer's share of overall revenue (their total over the sum across all customers). Keep the customers whose share is above the average share. Give one row with: the average amount those customers spent, their average share, and on average how much their share beats the average share. No rounding. A customer's excess is their share minus the average share, divided by the average share.
c.sql:
WITH CustomerTotals AS (
    SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS CustomerTotal
    FROM Customer c
    LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
    GROUP BY c.CustomerId
), CustomerShares AS (
    SELECT CustomerId, CustomerTotal,
           CustomerTotal / SUM(CustomerTotal) OVER () AS Share
    FROM CustomerTotals
), AverageShare AS (
    SELECT AVG(Share) AS AvgShare
    FROM CustomerShares
)
SELECT AVG(cs.CustomerTotal) AS AverageAmountSpent,
       AVG(cs.Share) AS AverageShare,
       AVG((cs.Share - a.AvgShare) / a.AvgShare) AS AverageExcess
FROM CustomerShares cs
CROSS JOIN AverageShare a
WHERE cs.Share > a.AvgShare

a.request: Total up each customer's invoice `Total`s, and compute each customer's share of overall revenue (their total divided by the sum over all customers). Find the average share across customers, and keep the customers whose share is above it. Return one row with: the average total spent by those customers, their average share, and the average relative difference between their share and the average share ((share minus average share) divided by average share). Don't round.
a.sql:
WITH CustomerTotals AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS TotalSpent
  FROM Customer c
  LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
), CustomerShares AS (
  SELECT CustomerId,
         TotalSpent,
         TotalSpent / SUM(TotalSpent) OVER () AS Share
  FROM CustomerTotals
), SharesWithAverage AS (
  SELECT CustomerId,
         TotalSpent,
         Share,
         AVG(Share) OVER () AS AverageShare
  FROM CustomerShares
)
SELECT AVG(TotalSpent) AS AverageTotalSpent,
       AVG(Share) AS AverageShare,
       AVG((Share - AverageShare) / AverageShare) AS AverageRelativeDifference
FROM SharesWithAverage
WHERE Share > AverageShare;

b.request: For customers whose share of total revenue exceeds the average customer share, return one row containing their average invoice total, their average revenue share, and their average relative excess share, where each customer’s relative excess is (their share − average share) / average share, with no rounding
b.sql:
WITH customer_revenue AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerId, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue
  FROM Customer c
  JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
), customer_shares AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, revenue,
         revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER () AS revenue_share
  FROM customer_revenue
), average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(revenue_share) AS share
  FROM customer_shares
)
SELECT AVG(i.Total) AS average_invoice_total,
       AVG(cs.revenue_share) AS average_revenue_share,
       AVG((cs.revenue_share - a.share) / a.share) AS average_relative_excess_share
FROM customer_shares cs
JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = cs.CustomerId
CROSS JOIN average_share a
WHERE cs.revenue_share > a.share

d.request: For each customer, total their invoice amounts and calculate their share of overall revenue. Keep only customers whose share exceeds the average share. Report one row with their average total spend, average share, and average relative excess, where relative excess is (customer share − average share) ÷ average share. Do not round.
d.sql:
WITH customer_revenue AS (
  SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total_spend
  FROM Customer c
  LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
), customer_shares AS (
  SELECT total_spend,
         total_spend / NULLIF(SUM(total_spend) OVER (), 0) AS revenue_share
  FROM customer_revenue
), average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(revenue_share) AS avg_share
  FROM customer_shares
)
SELECT AVG(cs.total_spend) AS average_total_spend,
       AVG(cs.revenue_share) AS average_share,
       AVG((cs.revenue_share - a.avg_share) / NULLIF(a.avg_share, 0)) AS average_relative_excess
FROM customer_shares cs
CROSS JOIN average_share a
WHERE cs.revenue_share > a.avg_share;
